name: Phone and laptop repair
summary: How expats find trustworthy phone and laptop repair in Singapore for cracked screens, liquid damage, and warranty-era devices — authorised service vs independent shops, data safety, and claim paperwork.
body:
Devices fail on humid commutes and Grab rides alike. Singapore offers brand authorised service centres, carrier shops, and dense independent repair malls. Choosing wrong can void warranty or cost a wiped drive.

## Authorised vs independent
- **Authorised** — preserves warranty, genuine parts, slower peak queues; bring proof of purchase
- **Independent** — faster screen jobs and out-of-warranty laptops; quality varies; ask about parts grade and water-resistance expectations after open repairs
- **Insurance / corporate MDM** — employer laptops may require approved vendors only

For phones still under manufacturer warranty, unauthorised battery/screen work can void coverage. Liquid damage is often excluded regardless.

## Data first
Back up before any repair. Decline “we’ll reset” casually if you need contents. For trade-in or recycle, factory reset and remove eSIM/Fintech tokens. Keep serial numbers photographed.

## How to choose
Prefer shops that itemise diagnostics fees, give written quotes, and explain refurbished vs new parts. Mall clusters allow comparison — still verify recent reviews for your exact model. Avoid street stalls that refuse to open devices in view for “privacy” without paperwork.

## Practical tip
If you just landed, check whether your home-country warranty has regional service. Parallel-import devices sometimes face authorised-centre refusal — know your channel before promising a same-day fix to your employer.
whenToEngage: Cracked screen or liquid damage on phone/laptop
Deciding authorised warranty service vs indie shop
Employer device needs approved repair vendor
Quoted repair without parts grade or data backup plan
